label: Luke 15:1
text: Now all the tax collectors and sinners were coming close to him to hear him.

label: Luke 15:2
text: The Pharisees and the scribes murmured, saying, “This man welcomes sinners, and eats with them.”

label: Luke 15:3
text: He told them this parable.

label: Luke 15:4
text: “Which of you men, if you had one hundred sheep, and lost one of them, wouldn’t leave the ninety-nine in the wilderness, and go after the one that was lost, until he found it?

label: Luke 15:5
text: When he has found it, he carries it on his shoulders, rejoicing.

label: Luke 15:6
text: When he comes home, he calls together his friends and his neighbors, saying to them, ‘Rejoice with me, for I have found my sheep which was lost!’

label: Luke 15:7
text: I tell you that even so there will be more joy in heaven over one sinner who repents, than over ninety-nine righteous people who need no repentance.

label: Luke 15:8
text:
Or what woman, if she had ten drachma
coins, if she lost one drachma coin, wouldn’t light a lamp, sweep the house, and seek diligently until she found it?

label: Luke 15:9
text: When she has found it, she calls together her friends and neighbors, saying, ‘Rejoice with me, for I have found the drachma which I had lost.’

label: Luke 15:10
text: Even so, I tell you, there is joy in the presence of the angels of God over one sinner repenting.”

label: Luke 15:11
text:
He said,
“A certain man had two sons.

label: Luke 15:12
text: The younger of them said to his father, ‘Father, give me my share of your property.’ He divided his livelihood between them.

label: Luke 15:13
text: Not many days after, the younger son gathered all of this together and traveled into a far country. There he wasted his property with riotous living.

label: Luke 15:14
text: When he had spent all of it, there arose a severe famine in that country, and he began to be in need.

label: Luke 15:15
text: He went and joined himself to one of the citizens of that country, and he sent him into his fields to feed pigs.

label: Luke 15:16
text: He wanted to fill his belly with the husks that the pigs ate, but no one gave him any.

label: Luke 15:17
text: But when he came to himself he said, ‘How many hired servants of my father’s have bread enough to spare, and I’m dying with hunger!

label: Luke 15:18
text: I will get up and go to my father, and will tell him, “Father, I have sinned against heaven, and in your sight.

label: Luke 15:19
text: I am no more worthy to be called your son. Make me as one of your hired servants.”’

label: Luke 15:20
text: “He arose, and came to his father. But while he was still far off, his father saw him, and was moved with compassion, and ran, and fell on his neck, and kissed him.

label: Luke 15:21
text: The son said to him, ‘Father, I have sinned against heaven, and in your sight. I am no longer worthy to be called your son.’

variants.reading: ποίησόν με ὡς ἕνα τῶν μισθίων σου ('Make me as one of your hired servants') is absent
variants.note: The fetched Wikipedia 'Textual variants in the Gospel of Luke' records for Luke 15:21 that the clause (present in Westcott and Hort and NA27/UBS4) is 'omitted by Byzantine text-type, and other Alexandrian mss'; no manuscript node of this graph is named, so attested_by is left empty. The WEB prints the clause.

label: Luke 15:22
text: “But the father said to his servants, ‘Bring out the best robe, and put it on him. Put a ring on his hand, and shoes on his feet.

label: Luke 15:23
text: Bring the fattened calf, kill it, and let us eat, and celebrate;

label: Luke 15:24
text: for this, my son, was dead, and is alive again. He was lost, and is found.’ They began to celebrate.

label: Luke 15:25
text: “Now his elder son was in the field. As he came near to the house, he heard music and dancing.

label: Luke 15:26
text: He called one of the servants to him, and asked what was going on.

label: Luke 15:27
text: He said to him, ‘Your brother has come, and your father has killed the fattened calf, because he has received him back safe and healthy.’

label: Luke 15:28
text: But he was angry, and would not go in. Therefore his father came out, and begged him.

label: Luke 15:29
text: But he answered his father, ‘Behold, these many years I have served you, and I never disobeyed a commandment of yours, but you never gave me a goat, that I might celebrate with my friends.

label: Luke 15:30
text: But when this your son came, who has devoured your living with prostitutes, you killed the fattened calf for him.’

label: Luke 15:31
text: “He said to him, ‘Son, you are always with me, and all that is mine is yours.

label: Luke 15:32
text: But it was appropriate to celebrate and be glad, for this, your brother, was dead, and is alive again. He was lost, and is found.’”

statement: A woman could keep a savings of ten drachma coins and lose one of them; the drachma was a silver coin in circulation into the Roman period, roughly a day's wage.
label: A woman's savings of ten drachmas

statement: A woman searching her house for a lost coin would light a lamp and sweep the house until she found it.
label: Lighting a lamp and sweeping the house

statement: A father could divide his living (property) between his two sons while still alive, at the younger son's request for his share.
label: Dividing the living between two sons

statement: A citizen of a far country could hire a destitute man and send him into his fields to feed pigs; pig-keeping was practiced in the Gentile lands around Judea.
label: Hired out to feed pigs in a far country

statement: Carob pods (keratia) served as pig fodder, and a starving hired man might long to fill his belly with them.
label: Carob pods as pig fodder

statement: The best robe, a ring for the hand and shoes for the feet were given to a returning son to mark his restoration and honor in the household.
label: The best robe, the ring and the shoes

statement: A fattened calf was kept in the household and killed for a day of celebration.
label: The fattened calf for a celebration

statement: A household celebration at the return of a son was marked with music and dancing.
label: Music and dancing at the celebration
The silver drachma (Greek drachm, the coin of Luke 15:8)
date: minted from the 6th century BC onward, in use into the Roman period
found: circulated across the eastern Mediterranean, including the Levant

label: Carob (Ceratonia siliqua) pods used as animal feed in the Mediterranean
method: documented agricultural use of carob pods as fodder

title: Ancient drachma
excerpt: a silver drachma (or denarius), which constituted a day's wage for a manual laborer, would be worth approximately the same in modern currency.

label: Wikipedia: Parable of the Lost Coin (the ten coins as family savings or dowry ornament)
title: Parable of the Lost Coin
excerpt: Joel B. Green notes that "the woman described is a poor peasant", and the ten silver coins, corresponding to ten days' wages, "likely represent the family savings".

label: Wikipedia: Carob (pods as animal feed in the Mediterranean Basin)
title: Carob (animal feed)
excerpt: Carob pods were used as animal feed in the Mediterranean Basin.
